text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: P1 triggered: `audit-log exporter delivery lag` breaching SLO.
- Signal: `p95 export_lag_seconds > 900` for 10m (us-east-1)
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/auditlog-export/audit-log-exporter
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/audit-log-delivery-lag
- Primary service: `audit-log-exporter` (S3 + webhook sinks)

Rafael Mendes: Picking up. Seeing backlog climbing since ~15:55. `auditlog_exporter_queue_depth` ~ 1.8M and rising. Persisted looks healthy (ingest->store ok), export is the bottleneck. Starting triage.

Miles Thornton: Confirmed. `persist_lag_seconds` is flat (<5s). `export_lag_seconds` p95 is ~22m. So this is delivery delay, not drops. Customer-facing impact: any audit log exports to S3/webhook delayed; Console UI reads from store so should still show events (if querying raw store).

Sean Gallagher: Any recent deploys? Also check if one sink is stalling all consumers.

Nadia Rahman: Looking at logs in `audit-log-exporter-consumer`. Lots of `context deadline exceeded` on S3 PutObject. Sample:
```
ERROR export failed sink=s3 org=... err="PutObject timeout" retry_in=10s attempt=7
WARN  backing off sink=s3 backoff=40s
```
It’s retrying, but workers are basically stuck on slow S3.

Aisha Bello: Alert shows it’s concentrated on `sink=s3` (webhook lag is elevated but less). We might be head-of-line blocking if we process sinks serially per org. Metric breakdown:
- `auditlog_exporter_sink_latency_seconds{s3}` p95 ~ 12s
- `auditlog_exporter_sink_latency_seconds{webhook}` p95 ~ 1.2s

Svetlana Petrenko: +1, exporter still does per-event fanout in a single worker loop. If S3 is slow, webhook path also slows. We’ve talked about per-sink queues but not done yet.

Rafael Mendes: Mitigation path: add more consumers + reduce batch size? Or increase concurrency per consumer? Quickest is scale replicas.

Sean Gallagher: Scale consumers first. Also check if we’re CPU throttled or hitting outbound egress limits.

Caleb Johnson: On the cluster: pods are CPU ~85% and memory ok. No obvious node pressure. Network errors are mostly timeouts, not resets. I’m seeing elevated NAT gateway connections but not saturation.

Rafael Mendes: Scaling consumers. Running:
```
kubectl -n telemetry scale deploy/audit-log-exporter-consumer --replicas=16
```
(reactions: :thumbsup: from Miles Thornton, :eyes: from Sean Gallagher)

Deploy Bot: `kubectl` action detected by @Rafael Mendes
- resource: deploy/audit-log-exporter-consumer
- namespace: telemetry
- replicas: 16

Miles Thornton: While that rolls, can we temporarily disable the “S3 export for all orgs” job and keep webhooks flowing? Or is that bundled?

Svetlana Petrenko: It’s bundled in the consumer today (single queue, multiplexed). We can’t fully disable S3 without a config flip + restart, but we can reduce retry backoff cap so it doesn’t stall so long. Risky mid-incident though.

Kevin Osei: Any chance we’re retrying non-idempotently and compounding? (S3 should be idempotent if key deterministic.) Also note: we must not drop audit exports; delay is acceptable but we need to keep within SLA.

Nadia Rahman: Another lever: increase max in-flight per consumer. Current config says `EXPORT_MAX_IN_FLIGHT=32`. If we scale replicas to 16 we should clear backlog even with some timeouts.

Rafael Mendes: Pods are coming up. Queue depth leveling off (not rising). `queue_depth` now 1.85M but slope is flattening. Export throughput went from ~1.2k/s to ~5.8k/s.

Aisha Bello: Dashboard looks better. `export_lag_seconds` p95 down from 22m -> 14m in last 5m window. Still above SLO but trending down.

Sean Gallagher: Can we confirm we’re not dropping? Check `auditlog_exporter_events_dropped_total`.

Caleb Johnson: `events_dropped_total` unchanged. DLQ count also flat. Looks like pure delay.

Miles Thornton: What triggered S3 slowness? Any region issues? Worth checking AWS health.

Nadia Rahman: AWS status page doesn’t show anything, but CloudWatch for our S3 bucket shows elevated `FirstByteLatency` since ~15:50. Could be transient or we’re hitting request rate limits.

Svetlana Petrenko: If we’re hitting S3 request rate limits, better to increase object size (batch events into fewer objects) rather than hammering with more consumers. But batching change isn’t safe right now.

Rafael Mendes: Agree; mitigation is backlog drain now, then follow-up to adjust batching/concurrency per sink.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Keep scaling until lag recovers, then we can revert.

Aisha Bello: Lag now p95 ~7m. Queue depth falling: 1.6M -> 1.1M in ~12m. If we keep current rate should clear in ~20-30m.

Kevin Osei: Please capture customer comms impact statement for Support/Sales: “Audit log exports delayed; audit events not lost; UI/API reads ok.”

Rafael Mendes: Noted. Posting in #support-internal after we’re stable.

Miles Thornton: Any internal consumers (SIEM webhooks) failing due to delayed retries? Might cause bursts when backlog clears.

Svetlana Petrenko: Some customers have tight webhook rate limits. Exporter does basic backoff but no per-sink rate shaping. When backlog drains it could spike. We should cap per-destination QPS. Adding to follow-ups.

Nadia Rahman: Queue depth now 420k. `export_lag_seconds` p95 ~2m. We’re inside the 15m alert threshold, still above 60s SLO though.

Sean Gallagher: Let’s keep incident open until p95 < 60s for 10m + backlog < 50k.

Rafael Mendes: Agreed.

Aisha Bello: p95 just hit 55s for the last 5m window. Backlog at 38k and falling.

Rafael Mendes: Marking mitigated. Holding extra replicas for another ~30m to ensure it stays flat.

Incident Bot: Status update requested

Rafael Mendes: Update: exporter backlog drained after scaling consumers 4 -> 16. No evidence of drops; impact was delayed export delivery (S3/webhook) up to ~22m at peak. Monitoring for stability; will scale down after sustained recovery.

Miles Thornton: Follow-ups:
1) Add per-sink isolation (separate queues or worker pools) to avoid S3 stalls blocking webhook. (links to ENG-2488)
2) Add autoscaling policy on `export_queue_depth` or `export_lag_seconds`. (ENG-2489)
3) Implement per-destination QPS caps + smoothing to avoid burst behavior.

Svetlana Petrenko: + also DLQ visibility: we need alerting on DLQ growth and a replay tool. Exporter PR is already in flight but needs prioritization (matches audit-log-exporter/pr_232).

Kevin Osei: Please include in retro: confirm retention window wasn’t breached and we stayed within “eventual delivery” guarantee for enterprise beta. Also note any orgs with >30m lag (contractual threshold).

Caleb Johnson: I’ll pull max lag by org from metrics and attach to incident notes.

Rafael Mendes: Scaling back down to 6 replicas now that stable.
```
kubectl -n telemetry scale deploy/audit-log-exporter-consumer --replicas=6
```

Deploy Bot: `kubectl` action detected by @Rafael Mendes
- resource: deploy/audit-log-exporter-consumer
- namespace: telemetry
- replicas: 6

Aisha Bello: Alert resolved. p95 export lag holding ~18-25s over last 10m.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved (signal back to normal). Please file follow-up tasks and link here.

Rafael Mendes: Follow-ups filed/linked:
- ENG-2488 Exporter hardening (retries/backpressure/DLQ) + per-sink metrics
- ENG-2489 Delivery lag SLO/alerts + autoscaling hooks
- Action item: evaluate S3 request rate limits and consider batching into larger objects
- Action item: per-destination webhook rate limiting/smoothing (assign @Svetlana Petrenko)
Will schedule retro tomorrow.
